newsitem.title: GERMANY: German sugar plantings to start in March.
newsitem.headline: German sugar plantings to start in March.

text.p: Sugar sowings for the 1997/98 beet campaign in Germany are set to begin this month as soon as farmers can be sure of mild temperatures and a lasting dry spell, industry sources said on Wednesday.
"Plantings could be completed within two or three weeks but may take longer if they are disrupted by rain," a producer source in the northern key growing region of Lower Saxony said.
Seeds sales were in full swing and sowings on light soils may start soon but may be delayed to late March/early April on heavier soils, he added.
The 1997/98 area may slightly exceed the 516,452 hectares seen in 96/97, sources said.
"Land set-aside has been reduced and farmers think only few income alternatives are as reliable as beet," one said.
Sugar content last year was very high at 18.17 percent versus 16.73 percent a year earlier.
National sugar industry association WVZ said the first estimate of plantings was due to be released in mid-April.

Germany's key growing regions, apart from Lower Saxony and parts of Saxony-Anhalt, include areas around Wabern and Frankfurt in Hesse, around Heidelberg in Rhineland-Palatinate, western North-Rhine-Westphalia and central Bavaria.
